claims.claim: NextEra's structural role links rising electricity demand to regulated grid/generation investment and contracted renewables/storage; the proposed Dominion combination would enlarge the regulated asset/customer platform but is not required for the standalone causal chain to exist.

The principal successor bottlenecks are regulatory approval/rate affordability, financing cost, interconnection/build execution and integration; scale is beneficial only while allowed returns and project economics exceed those burdens.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Regulated utility infrastructure and contracted generation/storage directly serve rising electricity demand.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Demand growth supports investment across scenarios, while merger/regulatory and financing outcomes can materially change realized returns.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Generation technologies can substitute for one another, but grid delivery and dependable electricity service remain necessary human/infrastructure needs.

risks.risk: Regulatory conditions, financing costs or integration friction can absorb scale benefits and pressure customer-affordability commitments.

causalEdges.mechanism: more load requires dependable generation, transmission/distribution and storage capacity
causalEdges.falsifier: load growth fails to materialize or regulators disallow required investment economics

causalEdges.mechanism: shared capabilities can spread across more customers and investment needs
causalEdges.falsifier: approval conditions or integration costs exceed realized efficiencies

unknowns.unknown: Final merger approval conditions, realized synergies and post-combination financing structure remain unobserved.

claims.claim: Current execution evidence supports a functioning growth engine, but it does not prove that a larger regulated platform will automatically create superior returns; regulatory affordability, financing and integration remain the main falsification channels.
Backlog additions and regulated capital growth are evidence of activity and demand capture, not by themselves proof of future realized margin or return quality.

factors.name: financingSensitivity
factors.basis: Large capital programs and a major combination increase sensitivity to cost of capital and allowed returns.

factors.name: regulatoryConcentration
factors.basis: Regulated economics depend on multiple commissions and approval/rate outcomes.

factors.name: confidenceInflation
factors.basis: Scale and backlog should not be treated as realized synergies or returns before approval, construction and operation.

risks.risk: Merger approval conditions or customer-affordability commitments could reduce expected economics.
Higher financing costs can weaken returns on capital-intensive regulated and contracted assets.
Integration complexity can delay or dilute expected efficiencies.

causalEdges.mechanism: higher funding cost narrows spread between allowed/contracted returns and capital cost
causalEdges.falsifier: allowed returns, project pricing and operating efficiencies consistently offset financing pressure

contradictions.resolution: Both can coexist; scale may improve capability while regulatory conditions determine whether benefits accrue economically.

unknowns.unknown: Evidence does not yet quantify final merger conditions or realized integration economics.
